title: South Korea opened bidding for a free, unlimited AI chatbot for all citizens
content:
TL;DR
South Korea opened bidding for a free, unlimited AI chatbot for all citizens. At least 50% must use domestic models. Beta in September, full launch by year-end.
The "AI for Everyone" programme requires 50% domestic AI models. It includes a chatbot and a public-service agent that finds benefits and files applications.
South Korea’s Ministry of Science and ICT opened bidding on July 13 for a free, unlimited AI chatbot and public-service agent available to all 52 million residents. The programme, called “AI for Everyone,” would make South Korea the first G20 nation to offer AI to its entire population as a public service. Two or three companies will be selected and given up to 512 Nvidia B200 GPUs from the government, with applications open through August 11 and a beta launch in September.
The official bidding documents reveal the scale of the problem Seoul is trying to solve. Two-thirds of Koreans have already used AI, and 44.5% (about 23 million) use generative AI regularly, but the vast majority rely on foreign services. ChatGPT leads with 23.45 million Korean users as of April 2026, followed by Gemini at 8.45 million and Claude at 2.41 million. Only 1.8 million Koreans pay for AI services. The programme requires domestic models for at least 50% of the system, with other domestic companies covering at least 30% more. Selected companies must match government GPU support with their own funding. The programme runs through 2030.
The programme follows the deputy prime minister’s statement in May that the benefits of AI must reach the wider public, made as Samsung’s labour union was preparing a strike over how AI-driven profits should be distributed. The “AI for Everyone” initiative is the policy follow-through on that rhetoric, treating AI access as infrastructure rather than a commercial product.
The domestic model requirement is a sovereign AI play disguised as a public service. By mandating that the majority of the system run on Korean models, Seoul is creating a guaranteed market for domestic AI developers while reducing dependence on American and Chinese providers. South Korea is funding its AI ambitions from the chip tax windfall generated by Samsung and SK Hynix, and the “AI for Everyone” programme connects the semiconductor profits at the top of the value chain to the citizen-facing services at the bottom. No other G20 government has attempted anything comparable.

report.summary: South Korea opened bidding for a free unlimited AI chatbot for all citizens, mandating 50% domestic models, with beta launch in September.
report.background: Two-thirds of South Koreans have used AI, and 44.5% (about 23 million) regularly use generative AI, but most depend on foreign services. ChatGPT leads with 23.45 million Korean users, followed by Gemini and Claude; only 1.8 million pay. The 'AI for Everyone' program, run by the Ministry of Science and ICT, treats AI as public infrastructure, not a commercial product. It follows the deputy prime minister's May statement about sharing AI benefits, made as Samsung's union prepared a strike over AI-driven profit distribution. The domestic model mandate is a sovereign AI play, creating a guaranteed market for Korean developers while reducing reliance on US and Chinese providers. Funding comes from semiconductor tax windfalls from Samsung and SK Hynix, linking chip profits to citizen services. No other G20 government has attempted anything comparable.
key_points: The program offers free, unlimited AI chatbot and public-service agent access to all 52 million residents. Bidding opened July 13, with two or three companies selected and given up to 512 Nvidia B200 GPUs from the government, matching funds required. Beta launches in September, full launch by year-end, through 2030.

South Korea mandates that at least 50% of the system use domestic AI models, with other domestic companies covering at least 30% more. This sovereign AI strategy guarantees a market for local developers and reduces dependence on American and Chinese AI providers, turning public service into industrial policy.

Adoption data shows heavy foreign dominance: 23.45 million South Koreans use ChatGPT, 8.45 million use Gemini, and 2.41 million use Claude. Only 1.8 million pay for AI services. The program aims to democratize AI access by giving every citizen a free national alternative instead of relying on subscription-based foreign tools.

The initiative is funded by a chip tax windfall from Samsung and SK Hynix, connecting top-of-the-value-chain semiconductor profits to citizen-facing services. It also responds to labor tensions, following the deputy prime minister's May promise to spread AI benefits widely amid Samsung union strike preparations over profit distribution.
report.impact: For the AI industry, South Korea's program creates a massive guaranteed user base for domestic model developers, changing the competitive landscape against ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude. Developers must meet localization and public-service requirements, pushing innovation in Korean-language AI, government benefit navigation, and document filing. For global AI companies, this signals a broader sovereign AI trend where governments subsidize domestic alternatives, potentially fragmenting the market. Regular users gain free, unlimited access to AI as a public utility, reducing cost barriers and ensuring privacy controls under national oversight. The program also sets a precedent for other G20 nations, proving that AI can be treated like roads or electricity. However, mandatory domestic quotas may limit model quality if domestic models lag internationally, and the success depends on smooth integration with public services.
report.tools: Watch South Korea's leading domestic AI models, such as Naver HyperCLOVA X and LG Electronics' EXAONE, which are likely candidates for the program. Developers can also monitor open-source LLM frameworks like Llama 3 or Mistral that could be fine-tuned for Korean public-service tasks. For community-driven experimentation, Hugging Face hosts Korean-specific models and datasets. Government procurement documents and the Ministry of Science and ICT announcements will reveal selected vendors from August.
